correctness.rationale: The degree-two baseline is the exact square \(Q(\theta)=(\cos\theta+1/\sqrt2)^2\). When \(n\equiv2\pmod4\), the contact point \(3\pi/4\) kills both free higher harmonics and forces \(a\le\sqrt2\). Otherwise the explicit perturbation \(P_n\) is strictly positive at both zeros of \(Q\); continuity near those zeros and a positive compact minimum of \(Q\) on their complement give a globally nonnegative \(Q+\varepsilon P_n\) with first coefficient \(\sqrt2+\varepsilon\). The proof treats every integer \(n\ge3\) and makes no inference from finite sampling.

The mod-four obstruction is explained by simultaneous vanishing at an extremal contact, while the complementary cases admit a constructive perturbation. This is a classification mechanism, not a routine numerical slice or a recomputation of a known table.
